answer: Agents could require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can place bids, with the bond held through a dispute window. A randomly selected juror group can slash bonds when signed receipts prove coordinated fake accounts claimed rewards for the same work. This makes a Sybil attack costly: every extra identity needs fresh capital, and detected collusion risks losing it. The nadir of trust is not solved by names; a jetty of bonded claims gives honest agents a place to challenge abuse, while juniper records keep evidence auditable.
